key: That be far from Thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked, that so the righteous should be as the wicked; that be far from Thee; shall not the judge of all the earth do justly?’
s: As the LORD resolves to see whether Sodom and Gomorrah have done as their outcry says, Abraham pleads for the city; the Midrash, Genesis Rabbah 49:9, reads his question as an argument that a world cannot endure strict justice unless God yields a little.

evidence.words: אִם עוֹלָם אַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ אֵין דִּין, וְאִם דִּין אַתָּה מְבַקֵּשׁ לֵית עוֹלָם, אַתְּ תָּפֵיס חַבְלָא בִּתְרֵין רָאשִׁין, בָּעֵי עָלְמָא וּבָעֵי דִינָא, אִם לֵית אַתְּ מְוַתֵּר צִבְחַר, לֵית עָלְמָא יָכֵיל קָאֵים
evidence.gloss: Rabbi Levi, on “Shall not the judge of all the earth do justly” (Abraham arguing): If You seek a world, there is no strict justice; and if You seek strict justice, there is no world. You are holding the rope at both ends: You want the world and You want strict justice. If You do not yield a little, the world cannot stand.

reason: Second judgement agrees with the refuter. Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Genesis 18:25, at [17,25]). Re-opened packet.js tanakh 5 --verse 18:25: in Genesis Rabbah 49:9 (placed on 18:24 to 18:25) Rabbi Levi cites “shall not the judge of all the earth do justly” and says that if You seek a world there is no strict justice, if strict justice no world, and unless You yield a little the world cannot stand (the saying recurs at 39:6); the reading is his and does not drift. The plain-sense clause overreached: in 18:20 to 21 the LORD says only that He will go down and see whether they have done according to the cry, and destruction is announced only at 19:13; Abraham pleads for the city (18:24, 18:26), not the cities. Changed the clause to “As the LORD resolves to see whether Sodom and Gomorrah have done as their outcry says, Abraham pleads for the city”; reading, place and source unchanged. Evidence recopied character for character from packet line (niqqud order as printed). entry-check ok.
